source: Minchat Shai on Exod 2:21 (the Masorah's three; the two-count ruled a corruption)
claim_en: TZIPORA: written LEAN (no vav) — and the Masorah on it counts THREE lean, with the sign given (the giving here, the taking at the night-encounter, the wife-clause at Jethro's arrival); 'and there are those who transmit TWO lean — and it is a CORRUPTION (shibusha), for in the whole Torah, in the precise copies, it is written lean' (MS): the stream verifies the ruling whole — exactly three tokens (2:21, 4:25, 18:2), the full spelling's census EMPTY: the bird-name of Moses' wife thinned at every station, and the two-count Masorah dissolves under the collation.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 2:3 (the Ramah's whole-Torah rule on the ark-word)
claim_en: TEVAT gome ('an ARK of reeds'): written LEAN, no yod, 'in all precise books' — and MS brings the Ramah's rule from the FLOOD: 'tevat atze gofer (an ark of gopher wood, Gen 6:14) — lean yod written... and every such form in the Torah likewise' — and the stream's census seals the pair: the construct ark-word stands exactly TWICE in the whole Torah — NOAH'S ark (Gen 6:14) and the mother's reed-basket here: the flood's rescue-vessel noun returns once, sized for one child on the Nile — the same lean word, the world's ark and the baby's (checked; the readings' pitch-inside-and-out contrast named at the mortar-file).

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 2:10 (the Ramah; the old copy's variant named)
claim_en: MESHITIHU ('I DREW him out'): the name-verse's own verb — and the Ramah's spelling-rule carried: 'min ha-mayim meshitihu — FULL the first yod, LEAN the last yod' — the stream's token matches exactly (yod after the shin, none before the suffix; checked), the word Torah-unique (census checked); an old copy's record of a 'Yerushalmi' variant (the letters transposed) carried NAMED: the Egyptian princess names the redeemer with a Hebrew draw-verb whose two-yod arithmetic the chain rules to the letter — the name Moses wears through the whole Torah is spelled here once, correctly, at its birth.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 2:22 (the sevirin file; his own cross-ref to Vayeshev)
claim_en: va-YIQRA et shemo GERSHOM ('and HE called his name Gershom'): one of the Masorah's THREE presumed-stations (sevirin) of this kind — readers PRESUME va-tiqra ('and SHE called,' for the mother bore him), but the reading is va-YIQRA ('and HE called') — MS pointing to his own sign-list at the Vayeshev portion: the presumption class continues its file (the run's presume-until and presume-which, gen_72/73) — the letter gives the naming to MOSES ('for he said: a STRANGER have I been in a foreign land' — the reason-clause in the father's own first person), and the presumed she-form is carried named, never written (checked in-stream).

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 2:17 (the Ramah; the Hilleli; Minchat Kohen; a minority Masorah named)
claim_en: The rescue-verse's two spellings: va-YEGARSHUM ('and they DROVE THEM OFF') — FULL in our books, with a unique-full Masorah note, and the Ramah: 'full in most precise copies — though SOME Masorot transmit it unique-and-LEAN' (the split carried NAMED, the stream standing with the full camp — checked); va-YOSHIAN ('and he SAVED them') — LEAN yod 'in the precise books and in the Hilleli copy,' the Ramah and Minchat Kohen concurring ('full vav and lean yod written'): the stream matches both rulings letter for letter (both words Torah-unique, censuses checked): the shepherds' expulsion written full, Moses' rescue written thin — the deliverer's first saving-verb enters the Torah one yod short.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 2:5 (Sota's dispute carried in the vowels; Saadya vs our books)
claim_en: AMATAH: Sota's dispute — Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Nechemya, 'one said her ARM, one said her MAIDSERVANT' — is carried in the POINTING itself, and MS lays out the grammar of each camp: the arm-reading requires alef with PATACH and mem DAGESHED (so Saadya's text, so the Targum's sense); the maid-reading takes alef with CHATAF-PATACH and mem SOFT — 'as it is in OUR books' (Rashi, Ibn Ezra, Chizkuni): the stream verifies our-books' camp exactly (chataf-patach present, no dot in the mem — checked): the hand that took the ark is decided by half a vowel, and the split is carried named, never merged.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 2:9 (the Ramah's five nursing-words; the Hilleli; Chizkuni; Ibn Ezra)
claim_en: The NURSING FILE: ve-HENIQIHU ('and NURSE him') — the qof with CHIRIQ 'in precise books' (Chizkuni, Minchat Kohen, Ibn Ezra — checked in-stream), and lean of its latter yods 'in the Hilleli' — and MS unrolls the Ramah's whole file of the nursing-tongue's FIVE full words: Sarah's announcement written FULL-OF-FULL with two yods ('would Sarah NURSE children,' Gen 21:7), the nursing camels of the tribute, Deborah REBEKAH'S NURSE, and the two of this verse — the princess's imperative with one yod before the nun, the mother's deed (va-TENIQEHU) with one yod before the qof (both skeletons checked): the Torah's milk-arithmetic runs through five words, and the verse where the mother is PAID to nurse her own son carries two of them.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 2:3/2:12/2:14 (the Mikhlol; the Masorah's three interchanged; the mark-split)
claim_en: The chapter's letter-and-mark file: ha-TZEFINO ('to hide him') — the tzadi DAGESHED 'for splendor' (the Mikhlol's weight-class; the for-splendor dot the run has met at the obedience-words) — and the Masorah's THREE interchanged dagesh-and-soft words named (the hiding here, the sanctuary-word, Samson's two-eyes plea: where the second letter should be soft and the third dotted, the order flips); GOME with the gimel dageshed (checked); va-CHEMAR with the bet SOFT — because the pronoun-he of va-tachmerah is QUIESCENT by the Masorah (Radak's Mikhlol twice): no sounded-he, no dot; ki en ish (2:12) — the precise books hang the ki on a GALGAL, not a joining-stroke: the galgal-vs-munach class's next station (the stream reads the joining munach — the split carried named, the accents-as-arbiters file); ha-le-HARGENI (2:14) — the lamed SOFT and the he without the little-stroke (the Mikhlol's folio cited; checked): six rulings, every one landing on the stream's own letters.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 2:1 (the Masorah's pair)
claim_en: va-YELEKH ISH ('and a man WENT'): the walking-pair — this verse and Ruth's ('and a man went from Bethlehem of Judah,' Ruth 1:1) — and the Kitzur's frame: 'by THIS walking came the FIRST redeemer; by THAT walking will come the LAST redeemer, Messiah son of David' — the Torah-side census verifies the phrase's uniqueness here (the adjacency's one Torah station, checked): a Levite's unnamed walk to an unnamed wife opens the redeemer's file, and the chain reads the whole arc of redemption between two identical steps.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 2:2 (the Masorah's four; Sota's arithmetic)
claim_en: YERACHIM ('MONTHS'): the Masorah's four stations — the three hidden months here, the moons'-yield of Joseph's blessing (Deut 33:14), and Job's two (the counted months that do not come; the months fulfilled — named): the Kitzur carries Sota's arithmetic on the hiding — the Egyptians counted her NINE months from the remarriage, but she had conceived THREE months before, 'and this is: they count the months to know her time — and they could not' — the three-month head start IS the three months of hiding (2:2's shelosha yerachim): the Torah-side pair verifies exact (checked), and the chapter's first number is a censor's miscount.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 2:3 (the two could-nots; the reed-vessel three)
claim_en: ve-LO YAKHLA od hatzfino ('and she COULD NOT hide him longer'): the could-not pair — exactly two in the Torah (checked): 'the land COULD NOT bear them' (Esau and Jacob's herds, Gen 36:7) and the mother here — the Kitzur's cave-midrash named (she dug for him even under the ground, 'for they knew the redeemer would come from there'); and GOME the reed — the Masorah's three: the basket here, Isaiah's reed-vessels on the waters ('even by SEA He sent an envoy — Pharaoh's daughter, to save a reed-vessel' — the Kitzur's reversal of the ambassador-verse), and Job's 'can the reed grow' (the Job-in-Moses'-days hint named): Torah-side the reed stands once (checked in-script): the weakest plant in Scripture carries the heaviest cargo.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 2:5 (the final letters; the maidens' three)
claim_en: va-TERED bat PARO ('and Pharaoh's daughter WENT DOWN'): the FINAL LETTERS of the three words spell DATAH ('her law/faith') — 'teaching that she changed her law: she went down to immerse, to convert' (checked mechanically — the descent-verse's own letters carry the conversion); u-naaroteha ('and her MAIDENS'): the Masorah's three — REBEKAH'S maidens rising to go (Gen 24:61 — 'she seized the deeds of the mothers'), the princess here, and Esther's (the fasting maidens — named): the Torah-side pair exact (checked); the Kitzur's darker thread named-only: the maidens who barred the taking, and the striking angel — the bath-descent that the chain reads as a border-crossing.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 2:2/6/7/13/16; Minchat Shai on 2:2/2:9/2:23 (named-only files)
claim_en: The chapter's named-only files, with one letter-check: the common tongue ERRS in quoting 2:9 — 'people mistake it and SAY et' — but the letter runs va-tiqach ha-isha ha-YELED with NO object-marker between the woman and the child (the adjacency checked: the taking-clause's bare joint is the Torah's only woman-child pairing): MS's note against the mouths, verified in-stream; the REJECTED LARGE TET (2:2 'ki TOV hu' — MS: found in ONE manuscript alphabet-list alone, 'differing from our Masorah's text' — the run's rejected-large file continues, carried as a rejection); the FIVE CROWNS on the good-word (2:2, the tagin — letter-ornament beyond the stream's reach: 'destined to receive the five fifths of Torah, the GOOD taking' — named); naar bokhe in gematria 'this is Aaron the priest' (2:6 — the brother stationed at the basket, named); ha-ELEKH three ('shall I go' — Miriam's word here, David's two: 'the prophets' words stand like the Urim' — her prophecy named; Torah-side unique, asserted); NITZIM three (2:13 — the striving pair; Sennacherib's ruin-heaps: 'the wicked are made desolation' — Datan and Abiram named; Torah-side unique, asserted); u-le-KHOHEN three (2:16 — the priest of Midian; Micah's father-and-priest pair: Jethro's history and Jonathan son of Gershom named, 'the fault hung on the faulted'; Torah-side unique, asserted); and the OPEN SECTION at 2:23 ('vayehi ba-yamim ha-rabim' — MS: an open paragraph, 'and the printers erred' — paragraphing beyond the stream's token-layer, named).
